findings.claim: The assessment blueprint commits the substance of both coding items (the exact validation/ProblemDetail task and repository-query/DTO task). The intake repeats each task, expected behavior, test mechanism, and implementation-time allocation at lines 663-672 while claiming that no item or task is authored. This exceeds the allowed blueprint boundary of objectives, format, count, duration, resources, and general learner instructions.
findings.recommendation: Remove the parenthetical Task 1/Task 2 prompts from blueprint instructions and remove the task-specific sections and expected outcomes from intake.md. Retain only the objective references, format assignment, item counts, Standard 45-minute schedule, toolchain/environment requirements, and the explicitly open Fast timing. Keep authored assessment tasks, tests, keys, rubrics, and solutions in platform-only staging.

findings.claim: FT5 tells the learner to log the caught exception at WARN, but allocates no teach segment and no pre-application check for logging. This directly contradicts the intake rule at line 408 that every applied Fast-project concept receives an embedded teach-then-check and that skim/reference pages are not assumed read. Marking the fragment “practised, not claimed” does not make first use precede teaching safely.

evidence.section: Logging levels and logger configuration; logging is technical behavior that requires explicit instruction rather than an unexplained project action

findings.recommendation: Before the WARN logging action, add a short embedded explanation and prediction/check within the fixed 85-minute FT5 block, funded by reducing apply or wrap minutes; alternatively remove the logging action and leave logging solely in the preceding skim/reference block. Do not change the calendar topic or day.

findings.claim: Objective o1 can be read as promising that adding Actuator makes the database health-indicator status visible in the default /actuator/health response. Spring Boot collects registered contributors, but component/detail visibility depends on management.endpoint.health.show-components and show-details; both default to never.

evidence.section: Health Information — show-details and show-components control exposed information and default to never

findings.recommendation: Make visibility explicit: have learners read the aggregate health status, then configure component visibility (with an appropriate exposure/security caveat) before reading the database contributor status. Do not imply database component details are returned by default.

findings.claim: Objective o2 conflates Spring Boot starters with dependency management. Official Boot documentation treats the spring-boot-dependencies BOM (or parent/plugin integration) as dependency management; starters are convenient dependency descriptors that pull in a supported set of managed transitive dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Separate the mechanisms in o2: Boot provides curated dependency management through its BOM/parent and convenient dependency sets through starters, in addition to auto-configuration and an embedded server.

findings.claim: The per-increment command uses POSIX single-quote syntax around -Dtest. Windows cmd.exe does not use single quotes as grouping delimiters, so the apostrophes can reach Maven as part of the property value and prevent Surefire from matching the increment package. That conflicts with the stated macOS/Linux/Windows execution contract.

evidence.section: Running a Set of Methods / Multiple Formats — -Dtest patterns and package path syntax
Remarks — cmd.exe uses double quotation marks for quoted arguments and treats apostrophe as a special character, not a POSIX quote delimiter

findings.recommendation: Use a shell-neutral unquoted Surefire selector such as mvn -q -o test -Dtest=increment<N>.* (after proving the exact pattern against the authored package layout), or document platform-specific quoting while retaining mvn -q -o test as the single cumulative command. Add a Windows command-line smoke run before release.

findings.claim: The six approved Fast increments have detailed prose but no committed manifest or accepted artifact slot: the intake explicitly leaves the package slot open and course.json keeps courseLabs empty. Consequently their stubs, public tests, per-increment package selectors, 70-minute plans, and no-container constraints are not machine-addressable or lock/gate enforceable.
findings.recommendation: Before increment authoring, establish the repository-native course-level project-package representation (or an overlay reference to one), bind all six increments and their public-test packages to it, and bring it under lock, schema, T07/T14/T25, and lab-contract checks. This records approved delivery mechanics only; do not add or alter syllabus topics.

findings.claim: At least the Hibernate 7.4 HTML source is not byte-stable: two live fetches one second apart returned different sha256 values solely because Cloudflare injected a different request id and timestamp near the end of the response. The recorded raw-response sha256 therefore cannot be independently reproduced even when the documentation content and URL are unchanged.

evidence.section: A Short Guide to Hibernate 7; first live response, including dynamic Cloudflare tail
A Short Guide to Hibernate 7; second live response one second later, with a different Cloudflare request id/timestamp

findings.recommendation: Keep URL and retrieval time, but additionally hash a deterministic extraction of the relevant documentation section (or remove the known Cloudflare challenge tail before hashing) and record the extraction/canonicalization method. Prefer immutable versioned artifacts when available.
